blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines remains keen on exporting processed ube as it works to expand the global reach of locally produced agricultural products, the Department of Agriculture (DA) said. Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. clarified the indefinite ban on raw ube exports, likely lasting until 2028, applies only to ube meant for planting. READ: DA: Ban on raw ‘ube’ export likely until 2028 In addition, Tiu Laurel said the Philippine government is “100 percent or even a million percent” supportive of exporting processed ube in whatever form. “I want to clarify something: some news reports claim that I am banning […]...
